# Testing the generation of `Innovation`s

## Definition of epidemic parameters
In a population of fixed size, the \(\SIR\) epidemic runs under the following stochastic dynamics:
\begin{tabbing}
\emph{Xemovals:}\qquad\= \(S\to S-1\), \= \((R \to R+1\) \= occurs at rate \(\beta \, I\), \kill
\emph{Infections:}    \> \(S\to S-1\),   \> \(I \to I+1\) \> occurs at rate \(\alpha \, S \, I\),\\
\emph{Removals:}      \> \(I \to I-1\),  \> \(R \to R+1\) \> occurs at rate \(\beta \, I\).     
\end{tabbing}
The structural parameter of epidemic `duration` 
(a positive real number)
and the `initial1` configuration
(of `SIR` type) are given by
`julia` constants,
as are the per-pair infection rate `α` and the per-individual rate of removal `β`.
The population size is computed as part of the construction of `initial1`.
```{julia}
const duration = 2.0;
const α, β = 0.2, 1.5;
const initial1 = SIR(0.0, 5, 1, 0);

const n1 = initial1.n ;
samplesize = 10000 ;

println("Total population size is $n1.")
```

## Simulation and storage of results
A sample of random `Innovation`s (with no conditional removals)
is generated using the following (non-executing) code.
```julia
generate_innovation(initial1.n, duration, α=α, β=β)
```
Total numbers of `Infection`s with specified `infectee` marks
and numbers of `Removal`s with specified `target` marks are tabulated.
The logic here is as follows:

(a) a given time line \(x\) accumulates infections arising from contacts between
a `target` time line (must lie strictly below time line \(x\))
and
an `infectee` time line (must be at time line \(x\) or higher)
thus occurring at a rate \((x-1)(n1-x+1) α\);

(b) a given time line \(x\) accumulates removals arising from each of the time lines
\(x\) and lower,
thus removals for time line \(x\) must occur at a rate \(x β\).

```{julia}
#| echo: false

data = DataFrame() ;

data[:, "Time line"]      = 1:n1
data.infections          .= 0 ;
data[:, "𝔼[infections]"]  = [(x - 1) * (n1 - x + 1) *  α * samplesize * duration for x in 1:n1] ;
data.removals            .= 0 ;
data[:, "𝔼[removals]"]    = [β * x * samplesize * duration for x in 1:n1] ;
```

The results of the simulation, together with expected mean numbers, are as follows:
```{julia}
println("Accumulating counts from a total of $(samplesize) replicates.")

for x in 1:samplesize
    iv = generate_innovation(initial1.n, duration, α=α, β=β)
    data.infections = data.infections + 
      [length([z for z in iv.infections if z.infectee == i]) for i in 1:n1]
    data.removals   = data.removals   + 
      [length([z for z in iv.removals   if z.target   <= i]) for i in 1:n1]
end

println(data)
```

## Statistical analysis
The `removals` column in `data` is cumulative, so use a running difference 
to derive independent data.
```{julia}
data[:, "removals diff"]    = [data.removals[1];          diff(data.removals)]
data[:, "𝔼[removals diff]"] = [data[:, "𝔼[removals]"][1]; diff(data[:, "𝔼[removals]"])]
println(data[:, ["infections", "𝔼[infections]", "removals diff", "𝔼[removals diff]"]])
```
Now each entry in either of `infections` or `removals_diff` is independent Poisson
with mean given by the corresponding `𝔼[...]`. For these large means we can use the 
normal approximation to the Poisson distribution.
Note that from here onwards we have stipulated that `Float64` be printed to only 2 decimal places!
```{julia}
import Distributions: Normal, ccdf
using Printf
Base.show(io::IO, f::Float64) = @printf(io, "%1.2f", f)

data[:, "p-value (inf)"] = 
  2ccdf(Normal(), abs.(data.infections - data[:, "𝔼[infections]"]) ./ .√(data[:, "𝔼[infections]"]))
data[:, "p-value (rem)"] = 
  2ccdf(Normal(), abs.(data.removals - data[:, "𝔼[removals]"]) ./ .√(data[:, "𝔼[removals]"]))

println(data[:, ["infections", "𝔼[infections]", "p-value (inf)", 
          "removals diff", "𝔼[removals diff]", "p-value (rem)"]])
```



## An example using a larger population.
This repeats the simulations of the previous section for a larger population.
```{julia}
#| echo: false
const initial2 = SIR(0.0, 10, 1, 0)
const n2 = initial2.n ;
```

```{julia}
#| echo: false

data = DataFrame() ;

data[:, "Time line"]      = 1:n2
data.infections          .= 0 ;
data[:, "𝔼[infections]"]  = [(x - 1) * (n2 - x + 1) *  α * samplesize * duration for x in 1:n2] ;
data.removals            .= 0 ;
data[:, "𝔼[removals]"]    = [β * x * samplesize * duration for x in 1:n2] ;
```

```{julia}
#| echo: false
for x in 1:samplesize
    iv = generate_innovation(n2, duration, α=α, β=β)
    data.infections = data.infections + 
      [length([z for z in iv.infections if z.infectee == i]) for i in 1:n2]
    data.removals   = data.removals   + 
      [length([z for z in iv.removals   if z.target   <= i]) for i in 1:n2]
end ;
```

```{julia}
#| echo: false
data[:, "removals diff"]    = [data.removals[1];          diff(data.removals)]
data[:, "𝔼[removals diff]"] = [data[:, "𝔼[removals]"][1]; diff(data[:, "𝔼[removals]"])]
println(data[:, ["infections", "𝔼[infections]", "removals diff", "𝔼[removals diff]"]])
```

```{julia}
#| echo: false
data[:, "p-value (inf)"] = 
  2ccdf(Normal(), abs.(data.infections - data[:, "𝔼[infections]"]) ./ .√(data[:, "𝔼[infections]"]))
data[:, "p-value (rem)"] = 
  2ccdf(Normal(), abs.(data.removals - data[:, "𝔼[removals]"]) ./ .√(data[:, "𝔼[removals]"]))

println("Total population size is $n2; simulation uses $samplesize replicates:")
println(data[:, ["infections", "𝔼[infections]", "p-value (inf)", 
          "removals diff", "𝔼[removals diff]", "p-value (rem)"]])
```
In a sequence of 21 independent Z-tests there is just one p-value at about 0.01.



## An example using a still larger population.
```{julia}
#| echo: false
const initial3 = SIR(0.0, 15, 1, 0)
const n3 = initial3.n ;
```

```{julia}
#| echo: false

data = DataFrame() ;

data[:, "Time line"]      = 1:n3
data.infections          .= 0 ;
data[:, "𝔼[infections]"]  = [(x - 1) * (n3 - x + 1) *  α * samplesize * duration for x in 1:n3] ;
data.removals            .= 0 ;
data[:, "𝔼[removals]"]    = [β * x * samplesize * duration for x in 1:n3] ;
```

```{julia}
#| echo: false

for x in 1:samplesize
    iv = generate_innovation(n3, duration, α=α, β=β)
    data.infections = data.infections + 
      [length([z for z in iv.infections if z.infectee == i]) for i in 1:n3]
    data.removals   = data.removals   + 
      [length([z for z in iv.removals   if z.target   <= i]) for i in 1:n3]
end ;
```

```{julia}
#| echo: false
data[:, "removals diff"]    = [data.removals[1];          diff(data.removals)]
data[:, "𝔼[removals diff]"] = [data[:, "𝔼[removals]"][1]; diff(data[:, "𝔼[removals]"])]
data[:, ["infections", "𝔼[infections]", "removals diff", "𝔼[removals diff]"]] ;
```

```{julia}
#| echo: false
println("Total population size is $n3; simulation uses $samplesize replicates:")
data[:, "p-value (inf)"] = 
  2ccdf(Normal(), (abs.(data.infections - data[:, "𝔼[infections]"])) ./ .√(data[:, "𝔼[infections]"]))
data[:, "p-value (rem)"] = 
  2ccdf(Normal(), (abs.(data.removals - data[:, "𝔼[removals]"])) ./ .√(data[:, "𝔼[removals]"]))
println(data[:, ["infections", "𝔼[infections]", "p-value (inf)", 
          "removals diff", "𝔼[removals diff]", "p-value (rem)"]])
```
